about: Each requirement of the public readiness specification, split into parts with an honest status for the current product. A status is a judgement recorded here; the traceability check verifies its form, its evidence links and its consistency, not that the judgement is right.

requirements.summary: Chemical graph, scene, containment and external references live in separate namespaces and are compared separately.

parts.summary: Chemical graph and scene positions are held and compared separately.
One ordered scene tree holds groups and simple graphics; scene-owned directed references separately name objects, atoms or bonds without chemical semantics.
Several chemical graphs and pages, text and other specialized scene objects, and specialized reaction or style references.

requirements.summary: Atoms carry element, isotope, charge, hydrogen, radical and query information, each compared atom by atom.

parts.summary: Atoms record an element symbol (1-118), a formal charge in -8..8 and an optional isotope mass number 1..999 as drawn; values outside these ranges are refused and change nothing.
Hydrogen states are recorded and told apart as drawn: stated with a count of 0 to 16, unknown, or inferred (the default). Inferred counts are separate read-only interpretations.

Radicals (singlet, doublet, triplet, unknown), query atoms (any, any but hydrogen, heteroatom, halogen, or a list of 1 to 10 elements, optionally negated), query bonds (any, or a list of single, double, triple and aromatic), aromatic, dative and unknown bonds, and attachment points 1 to 4 are recorded, refused in invalid combinations with a stable reason, saved, reopened and undone. Recording is separate from the bounded aromaticity interpretation; matching is MODEL-02.7.
A bounded named valence policy reports additional hydrogens and uncertain states without changing the drawing.
A named bounded policy interprets cyclic systems and converts supported aromatic and Kekule representations without changing the input during inspection.
A bounded versioned graph identity reports canonical numbering, symmetry and supported recorded or normalized comparisons without editing either snapshot.

A bounded substructure search of one drawing in another returns every atom and bond mapping under a named model, compares query atoms, query bonds, stated charge and isotope, reads aromatic and Kekule spellings alike through the aromaticity model, and refuses what it cannot read or finish instead of answering empty.
Broader valence and aromaticity models, additional fused and charged systems, and query matching.

requirements.summary: Drawn stereo marks, chemical configuration, CIP labels and enhanced stereo groups are kept apart.

parts.summary: Drawn stereo marks (wedge and hash on single bonds with the narrow end recorded in the mark, wavy on single bonds, crossed on double bonds) and stated configurations (tetrahedral centers with three or four bonded neighbors, double bonds, and an explicit unknown) are stored apart from each other, set and cleared by three commands, refused with stable reasons, cleared with a neighbor change and reported in the reply, and kept through undo, redo, save and reopen. Statements only: these commands label nothing, check nothing against the drawing and compare nothing (reading a configuration off the drawing is MODEL-03.2, comparing it with the drawing is MODEL-03.3), and the commands themselves are not drawn (the web editor's mark gestures are MODEL-03.4).

Derivation of a configuration from a drawing: set_configuration_from_drawing stores the center or double-bond state that wedge, hash, wavy and crossed marks and one scene instance's positions show, on request only, idempotently and as one undo step, replacing the stored record of every item it processes (a configuration stated by hand and an unknown included) and writing nothing for an item it skips, or refuses with one of six stereo_not_derivable_* reasons. The rules (frame, sign, fourth position, scope) are Chemifree choices named chemifree-stereo-1; the pure rules for the mirror image, the flip and a changed neighbor order (mirrored, flipped_over, turn_for_order) are defined and tested. Nothing judges whether an atom is stereogenic or computes a CIP label, the command itself reports no disagreement (it overwrites the statement of what it processes; the comparison is MODEL-03.3), and no mirror or flip command exists.

Consistency inspection: the read-only operation chem.stereo (chemifree-stereo-1, separate from chem.validate, which stays valence-only) compares each stored configuration with what each scene instance's drawing shows, per center and double bond that is stored or marked, as agrees, disagrees, only_stored, only_drawn or neither, with a structured label_differs field for the one non-atom position, a stereogenicity_assessed false marker and closed advisory diagnostics (drawing_disagrees, drawing_not_derivable, marks_without_configuration, configuration_without_marks, mark_narrow_end_not_a_center, center_has_aromatic_bond, double_bond_substituents_same_side, wavy_between_possible_centers, drawing_weak_evidence, stereo_not_checked). It stores, derives and edits nothing, is bounded at 20,000 entries (resource_limit naming instance), judges no stereogenicity, computes no CIP label and checks no ring or strain plausibility; chem.identity and chem.substructure still do not read stereo; the web editor's indicator is MODEL-03.5.

Drawn stereo marks in the web editor: the bond-kind group draws wedge, hashed wedge and wavy marks (crossed is set and shown through the bond inspector), a drag or click makes the bond, its mark and the configuration the drawing then shows in one transaction (one undo step) with the narrow end where the gesture started, the click cycle, order changes and the inspector clear the mark or stored double-bond configuration an edit would otherwise be refused for, a configuration the service will not derive leaves the mark in place with the reason shown, and a status line tells what a gesture stored, replaced or removed. Rendering constants are stand-ins for the public BoldWidth and HashSpacing document settings and every other geometry is a Chemifree choice. Comparing a stored configuration with the drawing is MODEL-03.5; the editor has no mirror or flip, no crossed canvas tool, and does not update a stored configuration when atoms move. The browser smoke exercises the same gestures but is not an evidence check of this record.

Agreement indicator in the web editor: for a drawing that holds a mark or a stored configuration the page calls chem.stereo on its own (300 ms after the last change, one request in flight and one more for changes made meanwhile, none while dragging, none for a drawing without stereo) and uses a reply only when it is for exactly the drawing on screen, positions included (otherwise Checking the drawing... with aria-busy and no ring). The reply is validated strictly against its snapshot and refused as a whole on any mismatch; the outcome must be ok with chemifree-stereo-1. The result is a summary line, a Stereo panel row per item and placement, and a ring on the canvas for each item that does not agree (solid for a disagreement, dashed for a state with nothing to compare, named, no pointer events), with a switch that turns the automatic check off (Check now asks once) and one-click edits built from the latest document: Update from drawing and Store from drawing (set_configuration_from_drawing), Remove stored (null) and Update all from drawing, each one undo step with a status line naming the replaced or removed value. Only stored configurations are compared with the drawing: the comparison itself judges no atom stereogenic and computes no CIP label (not assessed, never worded as no stereo; CIP labels are MODEL-03.7). A stored configuration is never changed except by the user's click, and moving atoms still does not update one. The browser smoke exercises the indicator, the ring and the one-click edits in a real browser but is not an evidence check of this record.

CIP labels: the read-only operation chem.cip (chemifree-cip-1) computes R or S for stored tetrahedral centers and E or Z for stored double bonds from the current graph, on demand and never stored, by Rules 1a, 1b, 2 and 3 only (duplicate and phantom atoms, implicit hydrogens, mancude all-carbon aromatic rings). Every item has an explicit state: assigned, none, unspecified, unknown, ambiguous or unsupported with a reason from a closed list, and the outcome is partial with a loss entry for each ambiguous or unsupported item. A CipLabeler port with a built-in labeler whose answers the application validates; scope stored, stereogenic or named items; bounded by 20,000 digraph nodes per item and 2,000,000 per request (resource_limit), with no time limit (a documented gap). Rules 4a to 5, pseudoasymmetric r and s, heteroaromatic rings and axes or planes are not applied and a tie they might break is unsupported, never none; no claim of equivalence with any other program, and a manual one-version RDKit comparison is evidence only. The web editor shows them only behind two switches that are off by default (MODEL-03.7).

CIP labels in the web editor: two Stereo panel switches, Atom stereo labels and Bond stereo labels (off by default, not saved), are the only thing that makes the page ask chem.cip, and only with scope stored (never stereogenic, because the operation has no time limit), scheduled like the agreement check (300 ms after the last committed change, one request in flight, none while dragging). A reply is read by a validator that checks every required field and value and ignores fields it does not know (state, descriptor and reason pairing; four ranked positions that are the item's own; E or Z only on bonds and R or S only on atoms; the stored record, snapshot, model, rules, scope, diagnostics and loss entries must fit) and is shown only for exactly the drawing on screen; any mismatch (an unlisted stored item included; a well-formed diagnostic code it does not know is only kept), a limit or another error shows CIP labels unavailable with the service's message and no label. Only an assigned item gets overlay text on the canvas ((S) near a center, (E) near a double bond; text form and placement are Chemifree choices, not legacy behavior), as an overlay that is not part of the document or an export; each Stereo row with a stored configuration gets a CIP cell under the switch of its kind (label, none, unknown, ambiguous or not supported with the reason sentence, or not examined) next to the agreement with the drawing. A label describes the stored configuration, never the drawing, is never written to the document and touches no mark; no enhanced-group meaning is implied. The client check runs the validator, the view and scheduler rules and mutation checks of them; the browser smoke exercises the switches, the overlay, the panel cell, the refusal state and an unchanged document in a real browser but is not an evidence check of this record.

Enhanced stereo groups in the document: absolute, and and or groups over stored tetrahedral centers, with the number kept as stated (0, negative and omitted included; an omitted number reads as 0), the interpreted number and a display label computed and never stored, one absolute group per document, created and changed by eight commands in document.transaction (required keys, group and atom references, 12 stereo_group_* reasons with the command index, a 32-bit number range), listed in every snapshot as stereo.groups, left by a member whose configuration goes, followed by undo and redo with stable ids, saved and reopened, and reported in notes (partial) when an edit changes which centers are stated to belong together. Statements only: no ratio is stated for and, nothing judges that members are related or stereogenic, chem.cip, chem.identity, chem.substructure and chem.validate ignore groups, and chem.stereo says it does not examine them. The web editor's display and editing of groups is STEREO-01.2.
CIP Rules 4a to 5 with pseudoasymmetric r and s, heteroaromatic rings and axes or planes, isotope-aware and symmetry-aware stereo, mirror and flip commands, and a crossed-mark canvas tool.

requirements.summary: Advanced objects (tables, TLC plates, plasmids, polymers, images) keep their hierarchy, references, text and style.

parts.summary: All of this requirement: nothing of it is implemented.

requirements.summary: An XML document format is read and written with typed styles, ids and text, reporting what is lost.

parts.summary: Bounded CDXML rich read/write of ordered pages, graphs, styles, Unicode text, IDs and known references, with a consented loss-accounted single-graph editor projection.
Advanced CDXML objects, editor rendering and full-format interoperability remain open.

requirements.summary: A binary document format is framed with bounded lengths, nesting and references, reporting what is lost.

parts.summary: For the bounded CDX subset, the header, tagged objects and properties, 0xFFFF extended lengths, nesting, strings and references are read and written with limits enforced before allocation, byte offsets on errors and a loss report.
Other binary formats, and CDX content beyond the bounded subset, remain open.

requirements.summary: MOL V2000/V3000 and SDF are read and written with query and stereo fields, reporting per-field loss.

parts.summary: Bounded V2000 MOL/SDF element graph and SD data conversion, with atomic preview/import and source-index maps. Query, stereo and V3000 remain outside this part.

Provider-level V3000 connection-table core: logical-line reader with continuation, block parser, a core-subset writer (element atoms, bonds 1-4, charge, isotope, radical) and closed refusal reasons. It is reached through the operations by CODEC-03.v3000-wire; query, SGroup, stereo and collection meaning are outside this part.

MOL/SDF import and export of the V3000 core subset through document.import and document.export: record dialect detection, aromatic bonds, bond marks (wedge, hash, wavy, crossed) both ways with the configurations they show derived on import, the ctab request key (v2000 default, v3000, auto), V2000 bond stereo column writing, and accepted_losses consent for stereo a file cannot carry. Query atoms and bonds, dative bonds, stereo collections, SGroups, R-groups, V2000 bond-stereo reading and the web choice remain outside this part.
V3000 query atoms and bonds, stereo collections and the chiral rule, SGroups, R-groups, V2000 bond-stereo reading and advanced MOL/SDF features remain open.

requirements.summary: Reaction formats keep reactant, product and agent roles, steps and mapping independent of layout.

parts.summary: All of this requirement: nothing of it is implemented.

requirements.summary: Line notations (SMILES, InChI) are interpreted, distinguishing string equality from chemical equality and reporting loss.

parts.summary: Bounded OpenSMILES subset: branches, ring labels, dot-disconnected parts, isotopes, charges, hydrogens and aromatic atoms are read; recorded-order and Chemifree-canonical text is written. Invalid text is refused with its position and a specific code; every written string is read back by the same reader. The canonical form is Chemifree's own (chemifree-smiles-canonical-1, bound to chemifree-chemical-graph-2), not another toolkit's. Stereo, query and reaction SMILES and InChI remain open.
Stereo and query SMILES, reaction SMILES, InChI and other line notations remain open.

requirements.summary: Unknown objects and properties are preserved, refused or reported according to a stated policy.

parts.summary: For the bounded V2000 profile, unsupported chemical directives are refused and projection, metadata and interpretation losses are reported.
For bounded CDXML, unchanged opaque content is preserved; unsafe edits require explicit discard, and uninterpreted selected chemistry is refused.

For bounded CDX, unknown objects and properties stay opaque binary, an unchanged original is returned byte for byte, edits need an explicit discard, and content with no CDX encoding is dropped or rounded only with reported consent.

For bounded SMILES, syntax the drawing cannot hold (stereo, wildcard, quadruple bonds, extended ring labels, charges and isotopes outside the drawing's range, aromatic systems outside the aromaticity model) is refused with its own code and position; dropped text, atom classes and undetermined radicals are reported as losses that need acceptance.
Advanced unknown and unsupported objects across formats remain open.

requirements.summary: Selections and containment determine exactly which objects a move, delete or clean-up affects.

parts.summary: Deleting atoms deletes exactly the bonds that touch them, and undo restores both.
Sibling graphics can be grouped; moving a selected group and child applies once and undo/redo restores selection.
Further selection scope, specialized objects, grouping and containment beyond the current scene tree.

requirements.summary: Edits are atomic change sets with consistent references, undo/redo and revision checks.

parts.summary: A transaction applies all its commands or none; a refused transaction names the failing command index and leaves revision, content and history unchanged.
Each changing transaction, undo and redo adds one revision; a transaction that changes nothing adds none; an edit after undo drops the redo branch without reusing atom ids.
A write based on a stale revision is refused with the current revision and changes nothing, including an aromaticity conversion whose revision became stale while it computed.

Saved content and history survive a crash; edits neither saved nor drafted do not; an autosaved draft is recovered with its history; closing does not discard unsaved work without the confirmed revision.

Adding, moving and deleting scene instances, moving atoms within one instance, and the positions a new or deleted atom has in every instance are one change set with the graph changes: one revision per effective change, none for a no-op, undone and redone as a whole; refused commands change nothing.
Scene creation, grouping, ordering, translation, references and selection are atomic and restored together by undo and redo; deletion rejects surviving dangling references.
Change sets and reference rules for later specialized scene and reaction objects.

requirements.summary: Formula and mass follow a stated convention for isotopes, charge, scope and numeric precision.

parts.summary: A bounded model computes a Hill formula and, with an explicitly selected checked external dataset, average and exact-profile mass and isotope peaks for the graph, selection or components. Results name the data, charge convention and display precision; unsupported or incomplete input has no invented numeric result.
Further chemical property models, broader data conventions, uncertainty propagation and other operation families.

requirements.summary: Chemical warnings, parser errors and opaque values are told apart, and failures leave state unchanged.

parts.summary: The bounded valence inspector distinguishes invalid and unsupported atom states with structured warnings and preserves the source graph and history.
Ring inspection reports unsupported systems, and a failed aromaticity conversion preserves the graph, selection and history.
Other chemical warnings, parser errors and opaque values across the full requirement.

requirements.summary: Stereo group labels, partitions and omissions are handled per format.

parts.summary: Group labels, partitions and omissions, in the editor and for the two exports that exist: a group keeps its identifier and members apart from the stored number, the interpreted number and the display label (stored and shown in snapshots, 0, negative and omitted numbers as stated, Or 1 and And 1 distinct, one absolute group, singleton groups legal); renumbering and adding members are not losses, while splitting, merging, removing members and a member losing its configuration are reported; a SMILES export reports the consent loss stereo_group for all groups, a MOL export (either dialect) needs the same consent for groups, and CIP and identity ignore groups. No import reads groups and no export writes them, so nothing here claims a mapping to any file format.

Stereo groups are shown and edited in the web editor: the Stereo panel's Group cell and group list read only from the snapshot (id, label, kind, the stored number as stated against the interpreted one, member count, member chips), one-click make absolute, group as AND or OR, add, remove, merge, split, set number and delete on the selected atoms in one transaction each (enabled only when the contract's preconditions hold, a disabled control saying why in text), a plain sentence for each of the twelve stereo_group refusal reasons, the reply's notes shown as for other stereo notes, and a Group labels canvas overlay that is off by default, not saved and never part of the document. The page states that groups are not drawn into exported files, not compared with the drawing and do not change CIP labels or identity, and claims no ratio for any kind. Nothing here maps groups to any file format.

Group import and export in the formats that can carry them (V3000 collections, CDXML and CDX group numbers, V2000 and CXSMILES), the per-format numbering and its losses, and group normalization on import.

requirements.summary: Document settings and application preferences are owned, changed and saved separately.

parts.summary: Each document holds its own style settings (bond length 5-200 pt, line width 0.1-10 pt, label font among sans-serif, serif and monospace, label size 4-72 pt, which carbons are labelled, and the unit lengths are shown in; lengths are stored in pt). They change only through an edit that is undone and redone as one step, refuses out-of-range values with a stable reason and changes nothing, and are saved, reopened, reset to the defaults or the preferences, and taken from another document as one edit; files from before them open with the defaults.

Application preferences (the interface theme and the settings new documents start from) are kept per data directory, apart from every document, and written atomically with a revision checked across processes. A new document copies the preferred settings once when it is created; later preference changes never alter an existing document, its file or its history. NMR and general numeric precision remain unavailable.

A separate persisted mass display precision is captured by each new calculation; omitted fields in older clients preserve it, reset restores the default, and changes do not alter existing documents or prior results.

Other computation preferences (NMR solvent and corrections, general numeric precision beyond mass display), other document style properties (colours, text and caption styles, bond spacing, margins, page size), named styles and templates, the scope of automation access to settings, and rendering with the settings by the service.

requirements.summary: Requests are typed and versioned, with explicit compatibility and structured errors.

parts.summary: Errors use one v1 envelope with a stable code and, where relevant, current_revision and command_index.

Within one process and its replay window (the latest 64 successful mutations of an open document; keyed per document for edits, saves, autosaves and renames, per process for creates, closes, recoveries, draft discards, copies, deletes and restores), a repeated request_id with the same body returns the first reply without acting again, and reusing it for a different body is refused. A restart forgets every request_id.
The capability list reports features that are not implemented as not_implemented.

Operation contract 1: each request names its contract version, request_id, compatibility profile and operation; each reply gives an envelope, an outcome (ok, partial, error, unsupported), the document revision, a typed result, model_id, diagnostics with paths and details, and a loss report. HTTP and the CLI pass the request bytes to the same Application::execute, and failures carry the v1 error codes. The catalog states, per operation and per transaction sub-operation, representation apart from execution, with the follow-up for what does not run; an operation that does not run (every chem.* operation among them) is answered unsupported, never with a result. model_id is always null and the loss report always empty: no operation uses a model or drops content.

chem.aromaticity_convert computes outside the session lock on a copy of the graph, under a time limit (default 5 s, at most 8 s, set per request by time_limit_ms); a stopped computation is the time_limit diagnostic (or cancelled when its host cancels it), changes nothing, and is not remembered for replay (a stop is honoured until the result is committed under the lock, and the requested time_limit_ms is part of the replay comparison once a request has completed); a result computed for a revision that is no longer current is refused with revision_conflict. A time-based refusal depends on the machine; time_limit carries only limit_ms. Other operations have no time limit or cancel yet.

Model identifiers from operations that use a model or method, resource errors and cancel for operations other than the aromaticity conversion, reproducing observed behaviour under the legacy-observed profile, other adapters.

requirements.summary: A deterministic conformance corpus runs on a real runner and keeps not-run and expected refusals out of the pass count.

parts.summary: A runner executes the cases in conformance/cases against the shared application, one fresh data directory per case, and records passed, failed and not-run (pending) cases separately per kind; runs in which no case fails write identical records; failure messages may contain run-specific values, including data-directory paths.
The cases are authored independently of any other program's code or data.
Independent graph fixtures exercise reindexing, symmetry, isotope and charge distinctions, supported normalization and bounded failure.
Graph, stereo, numeric, scene, encoding and host comparisons for chemistry, formats and rendering; a differential corpus.

requirements.summary: Analysis and implementation contexts and their artifacts are kept apart, with checked data inputs.

parts.summary: Traceability sources name a relative path under spec/ and a SHA-256. Paths and hashes are compared with the spec only when CHEMIFREE_SPEC_DIR is set. The loader separately embeds the public personal-local context needed to verify its exact identity.

The public repository excludes private data, vendor material, executable engines and full spec archives; it includes the public personal-local context required by the loader. A policy and .gitignore exist; no automated check establishes this boundary.

A selected trusted registry verifies manifest and review identities, the personal context, path containment, and typed readers for the scoped active DATA roles. Independent fixtures exercise decoding and atomic rejection; aggregate registry membership and actual private payloads are not independently verified.
Complete implementation-context input allowlist, independent verification of aggregate registry membership and absence of dependencies on executing the original program, and future DATA profiles.
